* More story oriented rather than scenario-based. You have the entire world of Zoincailla built up and I want to see it
* More level variety: I felt a few of the worlds here were a bit samey (mainly the "factory" style ones)
* Tighter weapon focus: Many combinations don't offer anything unique. I would love to see more like the sword, shuriken, or electromagnet. There's always room for lasers and explosions, but I want different ways to blow things up
* A new playable character would be cool. Maybe something melee or trap focused?

It's taken me a long time to find the words to describe how I feel about this game. I had never really encountered anything like it beforehand, and i haven't been able to find anything that can quite match how this makes me feel since (apart from Sunfluffs, the second game by these developers, lol) But with a few years and around 200 hours of playtime, i finally figured out what made this game so special to me.

I have ADHD and Autism, which means i interact with people and media quite a bit differently than many others. Certain things are a whole lot more engaging. For instance, games that can trigger big spikes of dopamine tend to be much more engaging for those with ADHD.

Copy Kitty has that in spades: there's explosions and lasers across every level and environment, great sound design that makes destroying stuff feel great, and a banging ass dynamic soundtrack that keeps you glued to the screen.

Additionally, Copy Kitty has tons of additional depth to its gameplay and its world for those willing to dig further into things. I mean hell, I finished my playthrough of the main content about 20 hours in, and I'm still coming back for more! It's only recently that I've begun to master Boki's Drill Kick, working it into every level I clear. Not to mention all the lore present (The universe Copy Kitty is apart of has existed for a while and is still being built upon, through other games, art, and media).

Copy Kitty has the exciting gameplay to satisfy my ADHD, and the worldbuilding to satisfy my Autism. There's plenty of other games with both of those things though. Plenty of my other favorites have just as many of those elements present. If you look through my library and my most played titles, you'll see that on display incredibly clearly. This was what had been [b]bugging[/b] me for so long. Why did I enjoy Copy Kitty so much more than these other games?

From a recent write up of all the game's dialogue for use with [i]lore analysis[/i], it finally clicked. Copy Kitty is one of the few games I've played with a neurodivergent main character. Most of what I've been able to enjoy either has a MC that doesn't speak at all, or one that i can only loosely relate to, if at all. Copy Kitty is the first time I was able to form such a strong connection with the main character in a game I already enjoyed so much.

By asking around on the game's discord server and conversing with other fans (and one of the lead devs), I've learned that Boki wasn't written with that idea in mind from the outset, and that things just sort of ended up that way with how they wrote her. Boki doesn't really have any *specific* neurodivergent conditions. However, through my time following Boki's journey, it feels as though we share almost  the exact same traits. I see myself in her passion, her determination, her tone, her language, the list goes on. There has not been another protagonist before, nor since, that has been able to match Boki in how strongly I connect with them. 

This is my favorite game of all time, and I've struggled for a while trying to find out how much of me liking the game is due to its overall quality, and how much of it is due to traits it has that happen to cater to me specifically. It's made recommending it to other people difficult, since I have trouble finding what to say. 

For those of you reading that haven't given it a shot yet, Copy Kitty is definitely still worth your time. It has an incredible combination of combat, gameplay depth, level design, music, and charm, on top of an expansive world with colorful characters you can really get invested in. If you're lucky, you might even form a connection with these characters deeper than what you would've otherwise thought possible.

Incredible hidden gem.

It feels like the later Megaman Xs plus Mischief Makers plus Kirby. It feels like the kind of low-poly feverdream you only got towards the very end of the lifecycle of the N64.

The game's presentation is a little rough and technical. Story mode is a series of small arenas where you have to kill all the enemies, interspersed with a little bit of dialog. But the ingredients in its design soup are all very good, very flavorful, and it hits a kind of "eh, good enough" scuffed feel that causes the dopamine receptors in my head to light the heck up.

The basic platforming and projectiling is megaman, but like, you get your powers the second you kill an enemy. And while you can only hold a few power chips, you have a button that fires them all as a combined shot. 

The stages do feel kinda puzzle-y. You're expected to use the unique traits of the chips to attack through walls and power slide and hit switches and whatnot. But the combat feels good and there's genuine technical depth. The bosses are sweaty. You can sight-read them, and you can get creative with the fights. If you let enemies stick around for more then a few seconds they'll start saturating the screen with touhou attack patterns, but this encourages you to play fast and aggressive and honestly it works. I went into this thing with expectations medium and it surprised me with how fun it is.

I'll update as I play further. I think this is probably not going to be a super long game (although there's two playable characters,) but it's surprised me once and it could certainly do that twice. Based on the fundamentals of play and how solid the gamefeel is, I feel comfortable giving a thumbs up at this juncture. If that changes, I'll revise. I think this is an excellent pickup on sale, and I hope people will support the devs in making more.

Edit: Exchikkalibur is a better fight than Meta Knight. When this game is cooking, it has the entire gas range on high.

2nd Edit: The difficulty gets pretty annoying, but dang when you can actually use your powers the game is a lot of fun. I wish it didn't spend most of its time preventing you from using your powers, as the frustrating part of a level is almost always the first bit where you have to kunai + kick your way into a viable build, but the game's high points make up for its lows.
It's a really fun game!

[h1]컨텐츠 밀도가 높은 수작 액션 게임[/h1]

평점 : 8/10
플레이타임 : 5h(주인공 봇키 메인스토리(노말) 클리어 기준)

장점
+ 다양한 컨텐츠(다양한 무기, 무기 조합, 다양한 컨셉의 스테이지들, 특수한 기믹을 가진 요소들)
+ 난이도나 캐릭터 변경시 고유의 무기, 무기조합이나 새로운 몬스터, 새 패턴등이 추가됨.(하드모드는 단순히 수치만 변경한게 아님.)
+ 스테이지 하나하나가 굵고 짧아서 가볍게 하기 좋음.

단점
- 이펙트에 투명도가 없어서 눈이 아플 수 있으며 공격 이펙트에 의해 적이 가려지기도 함.
- 기본 공격이 너무 허약해서 능력을 얻지 못한 순간은 게임이 다소 루즈함.

  카피 키티는 짧고 굵은 스테이지를 하나 하나씩 클리어해나가는 일직선 진행방식의 액션 게임입니다. 슈퍼 히어로가 되고 싶어하는 보키가 삼촌 사반트의 도움을 통해 가상 현실 프로그래매에 들어가 슈퍼 히어로가 되는 힘을 기르는 것이 게임의 주요 골자입니다. 각기 다른 컨셉을 지닌 12개의 커다란 스테이지가 있으며, 그 커다란 스테이지안에 작은 스테이지가 대부분 10개 이상으로 구성되어 있습니다. 이 스테이지를 하나 하나씩 클리어해나가면 최종 보스와 맞붙게 되는데, 이 보스를 쓰러트리는 것으로 게임은 끝이 납니다.

 카피 키티의 가장 큰 특징은 능력을 조합할 수 있다는 점입니다. 적을 쓰러트리면 적이 내놓는 10개의 기본 능력을 최대 3개까지 조합하여 다양한 공격을 펼칠 수 있습니다. 각 기본능력마다 서로 가진 특성이 달라서, 이 특성을 이용해야하는 퍼즐 성격의 스테이지도 존재합니다.

 또, 조합은 불가능하지만 매우 강력한 단일 능력들도 약 20가지 넘게 등장합니다. 이 단일 능력들은 비록 다른 능력들과 섞어서 사용할 수는 없지만 어퍼컷, 채찍, 다이나마이트같은 평범한 것부터 시간정지, 얼음블록 소환과 같은 강렬한 개성을 지닌 것들이 존재합니다. 당연하지만 단일 능력들도 각기 저마다 다른 특성을 지니고 있기 때문에, 이러한 특성을 이용해야하는 스테이지들도 다수 존재합니다.

 게임 플레이는 이러한 능력들을 가지고 적들을 처리하면 되는 것이 대부분이라 단조롭게 느껴질 수 있지만, 개발자가 다양한 탈것, 특수한 기믹등의 변주를 넣어서 게임이 꽉 차 있다는 느낌을 받게 만듭니다. 비슷한 형식의 스테이지는 거의 찾아볼 수 없으며, '적을 처치하라'라는 단순한 목표를 두고서 다양한 능력들의 특성을 이용하여 스테이지를 돌파하게 만들어 게임 진행을 다채롭게 만들었습니다.

 또한 메인 스토리로 게임이 끝나는 것이 아닙니다. 플레이어블 캐릭터가 총 2명인데, 주인공인 보키는 위에 서술한대로의 플레이 스타일을 지니지만, 보키의 삼촌인 서번트는 능력을 2개만 조합할 수 있지만 조합 서순에 따라 공격방식이 완전히 바뀝니다. 거기에 기존에 보키가 탑승했던 것들을 서번트는 해킹을 통해 자신의 아군으로 만들 수 있습니다. 또한 아예 날아다니며 근접 공격대신 넓은 범위의 배리어를 칠 수 있고 순간이동도 가능합니다. 스토리모드를 1번 깬 후에 해금되는 하드 모드에서는 새로운 적, 패턴이 강화된 보스가 등장합니다. 뿐만 아니라 창작마당을 통해 유저가 직접 맵을 만들어서 공유할 수 있고, 보스러시 모드, 끝없는 싸움을 펼치는 엔들리스 모드등 본편만 충실한게 아니라 그 주변 요소들도 풍부합니다.

 다만, 그래픽이 다소 가다듬어지지않은 느낌이 드는데다 이펙트가 큼직한데에 비해 투명도가 거의 들어가지 않아 시야를 가리는 일도 있고, 대량의 이펙트가 터져나올때는 눈이 아프다고 느낄 수 있습니다.

총평
 다양한 능력을 사용하여 스테이지를 클리어해나가는 형식의 일직선 진행방식의 게임. 컨텐츠가 풍부하여 3스테이지에 한번 꼴로 새로운 요소들을 만날 수 있다. 다만 이펙트가 심한지라 시야가 가려진다는 점이 아쉽다.

Copy Kitty is a labour of love. A passion project with seven years of polish. The kind of game that we all dreamed of creating when we were young.

But is it any good?

YES.

The ability mixing system is incredibly fun, encouraging the player to experiment with different combinations and switch them out on the fly to replenish ammunition or handle different situations. The feeling of power you get when wielding a triple combo is amazing.

The controls might take a bit of getting used to, so I recommend checking out some of the alternate control schemes if the initial setup doesn't click for you. I personally turned off the Item Menu and Command Dodge, and changed the Item Pick Up input to Drop. But learning the controls is well worth the effort once you're jumping, rolling, kicking and blasting your way through hordes of Constructs.

The boss fights are a consistent highlight and only get better as the game goes on, with some of the later ones being extremely creative and unique.

I was also blown away by the sheer amount of CONTENT:
- Two Playable Characters, each with their own distinct mechanics and weapons.
- A Hard Mode for both characters with remixed levels, enemies and bosses, plus a new story.
- Endless Mode
- Boss Rush
- Marathon Mode
- Secrets Galore
- A Level Editor.
And that's just the stuff I can remember off the top of my head.

Copy Kitty is a criminally underrated masterpiece. It's the kind of game that makes you realize that you can make those games you once dreamed about.

[h1] Недооцененное приключение котейки: от комнаты до армагедонна [/h1]

Вкратце - игра очень хороша, смесь соника, мега мена, марио, кирби и других платформеров. Суть игры - мы играем за котейку (и не только) и можем красть способности наших врагов, комбинировать их и тем самым зачищать уровень за уровень, побеждая обычных разнообразных врагов и боссов, а также меняя ландшафт окружения.

Эту игру я прошел залпом за три плотных вечерка, однако за это время я увидел:

- [b] Разнообразие вообще всего [/b]

Врагов, локаций, боссов, оружия. Их комбинации очень обширны, все время находишь что то новое. 

- [b] Глубина геймплея [/b]

В роботов можно стрелять разными пушками по отдельности или скрещивать их и получать одно мощное оружие, можно прыгать на них, можно отражать атаку, можно бить ногами/руками. Можно отражать атаки врагов ударом рукой, что я тоже узнал в середине. И таких деталей в игре достаточно, ее интересно изучать. А ведь есть еще второй персонаж с радикально другим геймплеем.

- [b] Количество контента [/b]

Количество контента для такой игры просто поражает. Основной сюжет, дополнительные режимы, два играбельных персонажа с разным геймплеем, два разных уровня сложности. Есть интересные ачивки и выпадают карточки. Игру вполне можно полностью пройти за 50-80 часов. 

- [b] Сюжет, графика, спецэфекты [/b] 

Я засунул все эти аспекты в один пункт, потому что они правда хороши, но ничего прям удивительного вы не увидите. Однако, общий стиль в стиле Y2K мне очень понравился, сюжет понятный и прикольный, с юмором, а спецэффекты яркие   и выглядят даже сейчас очень красочно и сочно.

[h1] Игра определенно заслуживает вашего внимания, игру делало 2 человека 7 лет, и она даже сейчас играется просто потрясно. 10/10 [/h1]

Copy Kitty is a run-n-gun 2D platformer whose central gimmick revolves around adopting the abilities of your slain foes and combining them into more powerful weapons. Think something like Megaman or Kirby.

Where the game excels is in its sense of pacing and spectacle. Almost every one of the game's 128 main stages has you seeing new things, experiencing new mechanics, trying out new weapons or weapon combinations (of which there's over a hundred of), or re-contextualising existing mechanics to keep things fresh and fun. Each stage is at most only a couple of minutes long, so its easy enough to pick up and put down whenever you have a moment too.
This is something massive development teams with hundreds of thousands of hours of manpower struggle to do, so for a game that was mostly developed by two people over the course of several years to achieve this really showcases the amount of love and passion that was poured into this game.

Other strengths of the game are in its charming story-light presentation and main character, a unique visual style that wields the early-00's-shareware 3D aesthetic in a charming way, and bombastic visual effects that punch way above the game's weight class with a symphony of explosions and colours.

The main criticisms I have of the game are threefold, and even then they're not that severe:
[list]
    [*]The flashing lights and explosions may be a bit much for those with more sensitive eyes. There are options to tone them down however.
    [*]The MASSIVE variance in weapon types and projectile damage combined with a lack of visible enemy health makes it very difficult to feel out how much damage you're doing to enemies and efficiently dispatch them. You kinda just end up spamming whatever weapons you have semi-blindly at the enemy (the game does encourage this mind you with how much ammo drops).
    [*]I would've liked it if the player had a bit more inertia to their movement. This is just a preference of mine though.
[/list]

A single playthrough will take you about four-to-five hours or so. and is honestly not that difficult (it is satisfying however). But you also unlock a hard mode by beating the game which remixes every stage and boss into a more difficult variant (it's not a case of just lazily upping the damage you take or anything). There is also a second entirely unique character with different mechanics to play as, as well as survival modes, boss rush, and even optional challenge modifiers. Heck, if you really wanna push yourself, try getting the gold star on every stage by taking minimal damage.

I would consider this a must-play for anyone who is a fan of Megaman and similar run-and-gun platformers, and a high recommendation to those who are just sort of ambivalent towards them like myself.

A young cat stands in her room. 
The core of Copy Kitty is light but intense action-platforming, in which you combine enemy weapons into ever-more destructive forms.  
Except *really* it's about obsessively replaying each level in the hopes of achieving the 'target damage' star, at which point it becomes a puzzle game about building the perfect combination of powers for each situation. Especially when played like this, Copy Kitty is one of the most engaging, finely-tuned games available - er - anywhere. The soundtrack is beautiful, the graphics are gorgeous and the story is touching. Highly recommended.

I wrote a review for this game a few months back expressing that I felt its game mechanics felt terrible and untested, and after months of this game rotting in my library I picked it up again to give it another chance and yeah I haven't played a platformer this unfun in my life. 

The whole game is basically just janky game mechanics bouncing off of janky game mechanics and none of them work well. Shooting enemies at any angle other than directly in front of you feels like a gamble as to whether the bullet will auto-target like it's supposed to or just go forward and do absolutely nothing, and even things that are super easy to get right, like the block-kick, are just extremely inconsistent. Sometimes the kick takes entire seconds to come out, sometimes it's frame 1, and there's no way to tell before it happens. This leads to combat feeling like few/no mistakes are actually your fault because the game just...ignores you sometimes. Rolling [i]exists[/i], I guess? But even though it gives you invincibility frames, it gives you so few that chances are you're just gonna roll into another hazard, especially considering the HORRIBLE level and enemy design I'm about to talk about.

Typically, levels in Copy Kitty are just enemy spam. Lots and lots of enemy spam. So much enemy spam. They feel like an AI generated the level, and leads to countless areas where 2 enemies are right next to one another, one being good at long range and one being short-ranged where it basically forces you to take heavy damage because you've been given no counterplay. A lot of the enemies are also incredibly tanky and/or have shields ensuring you can't hit them unless you're behind them, which is much easier said than done since the enemy spam is so bad that taking the time to run behind an enemy is a death sentence. And then for some reason the challenge damage is usually like 0?? Did the developer playtest the game with godmode on? I don't think a TAS could beat half of those challenges. 

Gimmick levels are even worse. Typically the gimmicks they show off, like bouncy enemies, just don't work half the time, and these levels show that off perfectly. They also serve to remind you that EVERYTHING you can attack deals contact damage because game design is for fools I guess. Slow-moving trampoline-like enemies? Contact damage. Targets? Contact damage. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WEAPON DISPENSERS? Contact damage. There was absolutely no thought put into this and it could not be more obvious. The fact you can die to touching a [b]WEAPON DISPENSER[/b] should really tell you maybe you're not putting as much thought into your game design as you really, REALLY should be. And keep in mind this is me assuming you're not being bombarded by enemies the whole time, which you often are. Just what I wanted in my tutorial level, enemy spam! To the developer's credit, at least it doesn't stick out with how awful the rest of the game is, too.

The bosses are more of the same. Crappy design, little/no tells for what attack they're doing, little/no counterplay to avoid their attacks, incredibly tanky, deals the majority of your health for every hit, you know all the hallmarks of careless game design. Never had fun with one of these.

For more technical issues, the game cloud saves you controller bindings, which would suck less if the game has broken Steam Input for reasons I can only dream of. This means if I ever want to switch between my PC and Deck, I need to go into settings and switch my controls around EVERY SINGLE GAME LAUNCH. Fun! Confusingly this game uses Steam Cloud's API too, which leads me to believe this isn't an error in setup but intended behavior? The hell were you thinking? Why would I ever want my controller settings synced? So that's great, can't switch between platforms without extra work, just another reason for me to not play this game.

And maybe the worst part, if the gameplay was made by literally anyone else, I would love this game. Its graphics and music are both fantastic and I love them to bits, and the characters are cute and lovable. So why God did it have to be spent on a game THIS carelessly designed?? Giant waste of talent. 

Furthermore, why does this game take up 3 GB? This is not a complex game. Risk of Rain 2 takes up an entire GIGABYTE less. Now I have plenty of storage so luckily this doesn't affect me, but it could very well affect someone working with less storage, and without justification it just seems like a huge, needless waste of storage.

TL;DR gameplay is absolutely god-awful and I wouldn't wish it on my worst enemy, and cloud syncing sucks too. I don't think I would recommend this game to anyone because I genuinely can't understand how a single soul could ever have fun with this. I really should've refunded the game while  i had the chance, but sadly I made the mistake of having faith in the game improving as it went on. It didn't.
